narrative:
The model estimates a 78% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability reflects patterns the system sees in your profile that historically align with employees who end up departing.

Three factors stood out most in the decision. First, your overall career experience of 6–10 years pushed the prediction strongly toward leaving. While many who stay have shorter experience (half have 1–5 years), your mid-range tenure signals to the model a stage where people often explore new opportunities. Second, the 1–5 years you have spent in your current role added further weight toward departure. This is actually close to the most common length of stay among those predicted to remain, yet the model still sees it as increasing turnover risk when combined with your broader background.

The only major factor pulling in the opposite direction was that you have not received other job offers while working here. Most employees who stay also report no external opportunities, so this element helped reduce the predicted risk somewhat.

Taken together, your experience level and time at the organization outweighed the stabilizing effect of limited outside options. The organization should discuss with you how to increase your sense of growth and recognition inside the company. You may want to reflect on whether your current path still matches your long-term goals. Addressing these areas early could change the outlook. (248 words)
